guia.what: A list of collapsible sections that coordinate with each other. By default, only one opens at a time; with `data-ts-multiple`, several can be open. Each item (`data-ts-accordion-item`) declares its `data-ts-value`.
whenUse: There are several sibling sections, read one at a time, like FAQs or specifications.
Showing them all open would make the page overwhelming.
Opening one should close the previous one to keep focus.
whenAvoid: It’s a single section that opens and closes on its own → `collapsible`.
They’re alternate views of the same object → `tabs`.
The content needs to be read in full and in order. Leave it visible.
dos: Write titles that say what’s inside. They’re the only thing visible when collapsed.
Leave the first section open if it’s one almost everyone will open.
donts: Don’t hide essential information in it. Collapsed content gets read far less.

teclado.action: Opens or closes the focused section.

nucleo: Each item is a `<details>` with its `<summary>`, so the browser opens and closes it—by click and by keyboard—even when JavaScript doesn’t load. Core only adds the rest: opening one closes the others, the event, and opening from code. Without JavaScript, each item opens and closes on its own (Enter and Space on the `<summary>`) and several can be open at once. With Core, without `data-ts-multiple` opening one closes the other, and every change fires a cancelable `ts:change`. To open or close from code, change the `<details>` `open` property. Core follows it and that change doesn’t fire `ts:change`. A disabled item carries `aria-disabled="true"` on the `<summary>`; without JavaScript it still opens.
